What has changed in Aziz since last year?
options: He is trying to be right rather than to win

fb.correct: 'Now you are trying to be right. It reads differently.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'Now you are trying to be right. It reads differently.'

1.say: Before you answer them, tell me their case as well as they could. That the money is better spent on the roof than on staff. Go further. Why is that a reasonable thing to think? Because a roof lasts twenty years, and a post lasts as long as the funding does. Good. Now you have earned the right to disagree. Much as I accept that, the roof does not teach anybody. That is the line. Put it in the report in those words. However much they argue about the building, the children are the point. Strange as it may seem, the sentence that concedes most is the one that persuades. Try as I might, I would never have written it that way a year ago. A year ago you were still trying to win. And now? Now you are trying to be right. It reads differently.

key: Good. Now you have earned the right to disagree.

1.say: Good. Now you have earned the right to disagree.

grammar.label: concession advanced — much as, however much, whatever the
grammar.form: Much as + clause; However much / However + adjective + clause; Whatever + noun
grammar.meaning: grants something fully and still disagrees

explanation.en: 'Much as I admire her, I cannot agree' concedes warmly before refusing. 'However much it costs' and 'Whatever the reason' concede in advance, whatever the value turns out to be. All keep normal word order after the opening phrase.
explanation.uz: 'Much as I admire her, I cannot agree' — avval samimiy tan oladi, keyin rad etadi. 'However much it costs', 'Whatever the reason' oldindan tan oladi. Ochilish iborasidan keyin so'z tartibi oddiy qoladi.

grammar.positive_example: Much as I would like to help, I have no authority here.
grammar.negative_example: Much as would I like to help, I have no authority here.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekcha 'qanchalik ... bo'lmasin' tuzilmasiga o'xshaydi, lekin ingliz tilida ikkinchi gapda 'but' takrorlanmaydi.

grammar.label: concessive inversion — Strange as it may seem
grammar.meaning: concedes a quality emphatically before the main point

explanation.en: The adjective jumps to the front: 'Strange as it may seem, nobody complained', 'Try as he might, he could not open it'. The pattern is fixed — adjective or bare verb first, then 'as' or 'though'.
explanation.uz: Sifat gap boshiga chiqadi: 'Strange as it may seem, nobody complained'. Tuzilma qat'iy: avval sifat yoki fe'l, keyin 'as' yoki 'though'.

grammar.positive_example: Try as she might, she could not persuade the committee.
grammar.negative_example: As she might try, she could not persuade the committee.

l1_notes.uz: Juda kitobiy qurilma; og'zaki nutqda 'Even though it seems strange' tabiiyroq.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Before you answer them, tell me their case as well as they could.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That the money is better spent on the roof than on staff.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Go further. Why is that a reasonable thing to think?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Because a roof lasts twenty years, and a post lasts as long as the funding does.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Good. Now you have earned the right to disagree.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Much as I accept that, the roof does not teach anybody.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is the line. Put it in the report in those words.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: However much they argue about the building, the children are the point.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Strange as it may seem, the sentence that concedes most is the one that persuades.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Try as I might, I would never have written it that way a year ago.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A year ago you were still trying to win.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Now you are trying to be right. It reads differently.
